question.text: Does immediate breast reconstruction compromise the delivery of adjuvant chemotherapy?
question.context: Immediate breast reconstruction (IBR) provides psychological benefit to many early breast cancer patients however concerns persist regarding its potential impact on chemotherapy delivery. We investigated the association between IBR, complications and adjuvant chemotherapy delivery. Retrospective analysis of patients in an academic breast service, who underwent mastectomy, with or without reconstruction, and received adjuvant chemotherapy. Comparisons were made between 107 patients who received IBR and 113 who received mastectomy alone. Those receiving IBR were on average younger, with lower body mass index (BMI) and better prognoses. Overall complication rates were comparable (mastectomy alone: 45.1% versus IBR: 35.5%, p = 0.2). There was more return to surgery in the IBR group with 11.5% of tissue expanders requiring removal, whilst more seromas occurred in the mastectomy group. There was no significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy.

medgemma_4b.clinical_reasoning: The clinical case indicates that there was no significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy between patients who underwent immediate breast reconstruction and those who underwent mastectomy alone. This suggests that IBR does not compromise the delivery of adjuvant chemotherapy.
medgemma_4b.critical_evidence: There was no significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy.
medgemma_4b.differential_considered: While complications like seromas were more common in the mastectomy group, the absence of a significant difference in chemotherapy delivery time makes IBR less likely to be a major factor in delaying chemotherapy.

rnj1_8b.critical_evidence: No significant difference in the median time to chemotherapy
rnj1_8b.differential_considered: While complications were slightly higher in the IBR group (35.5% vs 45.1%), the difference was not statistically significant (p = 0.2). The higher return to surgery in the IBR group (11.5% tissue expander removal) and more seromas in the mastectomy group did not impact chemotherapy timing. These findings suggest that IBR does not interfere with adjuvant chemotherapy delivery.

Complication rates were comparable, and while IBR had more return to surgery, this did not impact chemotherapy delivery timing.

qwen3_vl_8b.differential_considered: Concerns about delayed chemotherapy due to surgical complications or prolonged recovery were considered, but the data show no significant delay, ruling out this concern.
